sources.entry: Adium - Instant messaging application that can connect to XMPP (Jabber), IRC and more.

summary.one_liner: Adium is a free, open source instant messaging client for macOS (OS X) that connects to many chat services through the libpurple library.
summary.what_it_does: Adium is a Cocoa-based instant messaging application for OS X, released under the GNU GPL. Built on the libpurple protocol library, it lets you sign into multiple accounts across several messaging services and chat with people on them. Its features include tabbed chat windows, a WebKit-based message view that can be themed, Address Book integration, and Combined Contacts that merge multiple accounts into one contact. It also has an events system with Growl notifications, OTR encryption, file transfer, and Xtras for customization. The README says Adium supports 27 languages and lists system requirements per version, from Adium X 0.89.1 on Mac OS X 10.2.x up to Adium 1.5.10.4 on Mac OS X 10.6.8 or newer.
use_cases: chat with friends across multiple messaging accounts
send instant messages from a Mac
merge duplicate contacts from different services
how_to_run: Download Adium 1.5.10.4 from the project's download link (the README links to a download)
Requires Mac OS X 10.6.8 or newer on an Intel-based Mac for Adium 1.5 and later
notable: Built on the libpurple protocol library, giving access to many IM services
Combined Contacts merge multiple accounts into one contact
WebKit message view for themeable chat windows
OTR encryption and file transfer built in
Older Adium versions support PowerPC Macs and earlier OS X releases
caveats: macOS only; README lists system requirements for each release, and Adium 1.5 and later require an Intel Mac
README does not give a full list of supported services in the text; it links to one
Growl notifications depend on Growl, which the README mentions but does not describe further
